I'm not the type to just go sharing things willy-nilly with anyone who wants to look at it. My name isn't Hillary, after all. But I'm terrified of applying through these online systems like Indeed and Monster, etc. I found a position that seems to fit my strengths, qualifications, and interests, but 1) it's a state/government position (probably the #1 worst offender with snooping and data-harvesting), and 2) they don't accept paper applications anymore, it has to go through the HR screening software, which is called GovernmentJobs.com (a company they've outsourced their computer applications to). You have to complete a "profile" which basically consists of little more than just uploading a .doc or .pdf resume and filling in some other sections (education, references, etc.), that are almost redundant, because they've already been entered in the resume.

I don't want to just be applying for things all over the place and being "promiscuous" with my information. I don't have a LinkedIn or even a cell phone number, or even a personal email address. But I know beggars can't be choosers, and that's one of the things I hate. It feels violating, and I'm not one to go all SJW and call things "rape" when they really aren't, but it's still very discomforting to me, the notion that you don't know where your data is going and what's going to be done with it once it's in someone's system -- even if, or perhaps especially if, it's a state or government entity. It does kind of feel like writing your name and phone number on the wall of a seedy pub with the words "For a good time, call" above it. But my name isn't [Jenny](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6WTdTwcmxyo) either.

So should I go for it? Conversely, would I get scrutinized for *not* being a "data whore" with a zillion social media accounts or even an empty Facebook, as in it makes me look out-of-touch and even paranoid (the latter of which I most definitely am)? It's just an entry-level clerical position, but being that it's a state job, the pay is adequate, adequate enough for a singleton who doesn't have much more than the basics in terms of wants or needs, or any interest in having a family, or any desire to move up and expand my assets in the future. (Mid-$30Ks.) There's always a chance they *won't* call me back, what with the economy being bad and a Disney World line of applicants ahead of and in addition to me, but if they do, that'd be good of course -- and then with any luck I won't have to go through the process ever again. The opening closes on the 10th, so any advice would be greatly appreciated.

----------

**EDIT:** Forgot to mention that I know these HR screening systems do a keyword scan for "undesirable" words. But I can't lie and say I have a computer and business degree when all I have is "Liberal Arts." Yes, I know I'm useless, but do you think even a government system advertising a clerical position would blacklist applications with the dreaded L-word? Would they really require an engineering degree to do office work? It doesn't say so on the application, it just says "Bachelor's degree" but doesn't say in what. But with the bad press surrounding liberal arts degrees, I'm worried that I'll get blacklisted no matter what.
Should I apply for a job through an online system? I'm afraid of my information being in a database somewhere.

Leave out your address, social, and phone, and just enter Available When Hired Only, or something. There are tons of places that just harvest info, so you are correct to be cautious.

Try to contact them directly and go around the screening company. A few emails and phone calls could get you a direct conversation with someone who actually makes the decision.
If you're brought in for an interview and they decide to move forward, they will probably check your credentials. Lying about your degree will cost you the job.
